applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 30 May 1984, entered into force 1985)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-59 and R.561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT obligations, PEP framework and UBO disclosure duties); Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD) as transposed; Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 4 February 2020 on transparency of companies and financial operations; Décret n° 2021-1517 of 19 November 2021 (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs — RBE); Code de commerce, Articles L.123-1, L.123-33 and L.227-1 et seq.; Loi n° 2016-731 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each beneficial owner's passport or national identity document, accompanied by a certified French translation (traduction assermentée)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin and a court-certified translator (traducteur expert) in France, or the French Consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (apostille applicable where the origin jurisdiction is a party to the 1961 HCCH Convention; e.g., PRC apostille regime effective 7 November 2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency, corporate registry extract, or Certificate of Good Standing of the non-resident corporate shareholder (e.g., Chinese business registration extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official commercial registry or licensed registered agent in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank attestation of blocked capital contribution funds (attestation de blocage de fonds) or banker's reference letter evidencing lawful source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (apostille required if the banking jurisdiction is an HCCH 1961 member; otherwise consular legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Domiciliation agreement (contrat de domiciliation) for the French registered office executed with a licensed commercial domiciliation company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed société de domiciliation established in France
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (not applicable — domestic French document; notarized execution in France and mutual countersignature suffice)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against: (i) the OFAC SDN List; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) the French national asset-freeze list published by the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) and the French AML FIU Tracfin; and (v) PEP status under CMF Article L.561-10 including family members and known close associates, applying risk-based customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence where triggered, with an ongoing monitoring framework under CMF Article L.561-6.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with subsequent registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) effected by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Kbis/extract issuance via Infogreffe).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS dénomination sociale must be distinct, lawful, and not contrary to public policy; it must be expressed in Latin script and must be followed by the exact legal form indicator 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or 'SAS' in all formal instruments. A name originally in a non-Latin alphabet (e.g., Chinese characters) must be accompanied by an official French/Latin transliteration, which becomes the operative legal name for French corporate documents, invoices, and the RCS register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank — requires prior ACPR (Prudential Supervision Authority) authorization as a credit institution
Assurance / Insurance — requires ACPR authorization and is prohibited for non-licensed entities
France / République / National / Municipal / Préfecture — terms implying official state, territorial or public authority endorsement
Chambre de Commerce / Bourse / Fiduciaire — protected institutional or professional denominations
Société / SARL / SA / EURL — misleading alternative legal-form suffixes; only 'SAS' may be used
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not operate a stand-alone corporate name reservation ledger; name clearance occurs integrally at the Guichet Unique filing. Upon rejection or an adverse prior-rights finding, the applicant: (1) may re-file an amended name through the Guichet Unique within a 30-day priority window; (2) may file a gracieuse claim (réclamation) with INPI within 30 days of the rejection notice; (3) may apply before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce by référé procedure seeking an order compelling the registrar to proceed; and (4) in the case of an infringement action, may petition the competent judicial court for dissolution of the conflicting name or damages. No statutory extension of the priority window is available; counsel must monetize trademark and company-name watch results before any re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the statutory registered office (siège social) under Articles L.123-14-2 and R.123-167 of the Code de commerce, provided a licensed commercial domiciliation company is used, the domiciliation contract is executed for a minimum term and expressly identifies the SAS, and the domiciliation company maintains material facilities, mail-handling capacity, and a dedicated meeting room. For the ISIC 2750 autonomous robotic appliance manufacturing scope conducted on an OEM basis, commercial domiciliation is acceptable for the administrative seat only if genuine management substance — board decisions, contracting, invoicing, and customer-facing operations — is in fact exercised in France; otherwise, the registered office may be re-characterized or challenged for VAT, permanent establishment, and corporate substance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk. For a newly formed SAS in a low AML-risk tier, unannounced physical on-site inspection probability is estimated at approximately: 15% within the first 24 months for an URSSAF social security inspection; 10% within the first reporting cycle for a DGFiP tax audit (vérification de comptabilité); and 5% for a registry or administrative verification of the registered office. Any declared French manufacturing, warehousing, or logistics premises materially increase the likelihood of inspection; a purely domiciled administrative address presents a lower probability but requires demonstrable mail handling, legal presence, and contactability of the legal representative.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAS bylaws (statuts), legal due diligence opinion and incorporation file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — flat-fee engagement letter

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability and prior-rights watch (INPI trademark search and corporate register conflicting-name search)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) and/or IP counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff — INPI official fee schedule; plus market-based search report fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet Unique (INPI) registration filing fee and RCS registration fee at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff — INPI and greffier tariff orders in force

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory legal announcement (avis de constitution) in an authorized Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative tariff ceiling fixed by prefectural order; market average EUR 150–220 excluding VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation service — first-year fee with a licensed commercial domiciliation company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for commercial domiciliation in Paris or major French business hubs (EUR 100–150 per month all-inclusive)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille/consular legalization, and certified French translation of the foreign KYC bundle (passports, corporate registry extracts, banker's attestations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in country of origin, competent authority issuing apostille (e.g., PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs), French Consulate, and sworn translator in France
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff — French notary tariff decree; consular fee schedule; sworn translator's professional rate schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) preparation and PEP/sanctions screening compliance report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML/CFT compliance provider instructed through the French avocat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — fixed compliance fee per UBO declared

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II (Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 for Société par Actions Simplifiée), read with Articles L.210-1 et seq., L.210-6, R.210-1 et seq. and the general provisions on legal persons in Book I.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and filed through the INPI Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Cerfa N° M0 (déclaration de constitution de société) submitted through the INPI online portal for registration at the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal capital for an SAS. The articles of association freely fix the share capital. All issued shares must be fully subscribed and fully paid up in accordance with Article L.227-2. There is no statutory requirement for a bank escrow account for cash contributions, but capital contributions must be effectively available and supported by a certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage / attestation de dépôt des fonds) when the bank is not opened with a notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers present hereby adopt the attached articles of association, approve the share subscriptions, and declare that the entire stated share capital of EUR [amount] has been subscribed and fully released in accordance with Article L.227-2 of the French Commercial Code. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be established at [address], and that the President and any other officers named in the attendance sheet be and are hereby appointed as legal representatives of the corporation with full powers to act on its behalf in all circumstances within the limits of the corporate object. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the President be and is hereby authorized to complete all formalities of registration, publication, and governmental authorizations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French legal counsel or notary (optional intermediary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language articles of association for the SAS, including corporate name, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, share capital, share subscription terms, management powers, and governance rules. Verify the availability of the corporate name with INPI and draft the first written resolutions.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all shareholders and the President
Valuation certificate for any in-kind contributions (commissaire aux apports) if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the draft, simply amend the relevant clauses and resubmit before publication; any defect in valuation may be cured by a supplemental valuation report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Notice in an Authorized Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Support d'annonces légales (approved by the Préfecture, e.g., Les Affiches Parisiennes in Paris or the local approved gazette in the department).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place an insertion order with the approved legal-announcements gazette in the department of the registered office. The insertion must contain the proposed corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, and managing officers.
required_dossiers: Company search proof / name reservation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette publication contains errors, request a corrected re-publication before submitting the RCS registration to avoid refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing through the INPI Guichet Unique and RCS Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique operated by Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), which transmits the file to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online teleprocedure for company formation at guichet-entreprises.fr / formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Upload the signed articles, the gazette notice, identity documents, proof of address, the deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds), the beneficial-owner declaration, and any powers of attorney. Submit the dossier; upon validation the Greffe issues the RCS extract (extrait Kbis).
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association (dated and initialed)
Certificate of deposit of capital funds
Identity document and proof of address of the President
Registered-office proof (lease, ownership title, or co-working agreement)
Declaration of non-conviction and compatibility for managers
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or placed in abeyance, correct the flagged fields and resubmit the requested supporting documents within the electronic procedure. If the Greffe refuses registration, request a written reasons statement and apply to the President of the Commercial Court for a rectification order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Strengthening Legal Existence and Post-Registration Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and designated tax and social administrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Kbis extract, verify all registry data, obtain the SIREN/SIRET and TVA intra-community number. If not already filed, confirm the beneficial-owner declaration with the registry. Publish any remaining statutory notices and ensure statutory books are opened.
required_dossiers: Beneficial-owner declaration (if not filed at registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry data is inaccurate, file a request for rectification of the RCS record; failure to file the RBE can be cured by online supplementary filing before enforcement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Governance Meeting and Opening of Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company directors and authorized bank institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or shareholder written decision to ratify the registration acts, authorize the President and any Relevant officers to open a corporate bank account and borrow for operational needs, approve the accounting framework, and designate the external statutory auditor if the company exceeds the legal thresholds.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting or written resolution
Identification of the President, officers, and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or counterparty requests additional corporate information, execute an additional ratification resolution; a missing formal step can be validated by a later shareholder resolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) — Inspection des Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE), supported by the local DDPP/DRIEAT as applicable.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for the pure assembly and functional testing of robotic vacuum appliances. If the physical process exceeds the ICPE thresholds for surface treatment, coating, solvent utilization, or hazardous waste generation, an Enregistrement or Autorisation Environnementale under the French Environmental Code (Titre Ier du Livre V) must be obtained.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique through DREAL/Inspection des Installations Classées
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No mandatory EIA for low-impact assembly and testing. A case-by-case assessment is triggered only if the facility falls under the ICPE registration or authorization regime (rubriques listed in the nomenclature). The default classification is 'not subject to EIA'.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with the applicable ministerial order thresholds (notably for pH, SS, BOD, COD) if connected to a sewer. VOC emissions must respect the sectoral thresholds of Directive 2010/75/EU as transposed; waste handling must be performed by registered carriers with a waste manifest (bordereau de suivi de déchets) and the waste codes established by Annex II of the Code de l'environnement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Commission de Sécurité (or certificate of compliance from a certified bureau de contrôle) is required before opening the premises to staff. Structural load inspections must be contracted with a certified structural engineer if installing heavy machinery. Workplace clearance includes the electrical installation conformity certificate, the approval of ventilation and workstation ergonomics, and the labor inspection endorsement from DREETS as to compliance with the Labor Code (Code du travail), including first-aid equipment and emergency evacuation signage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) — French national tax authority; primary portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate online portal: www.gdfs.fr; company registry with SIREN/SIRET attribution: INSEE via the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); dedicated VAT registration platform for non-residents: DGFIP Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity establishing a French SAS: (1) file statutory incorporation documentation (statutes, proof of registered office, identity of legal representatives, confirmation of no minimum share capital) via the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises; (2) the CFE forwards the dossier to the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) for issuance of the SIREN company number and SIRET establishment number; (3) DGFIP automatically allocates a French VAT identification number (intra-community FR TVA number) and the standard corporate taxpayer reference; (4) the SAS must file a 'déclaration d'existence' (form M0 variant) within one month of incorporation and register for Corporation Tax (IS) and VAT with the local Entreprise (SIE) in the competent territorial department; (5) for non-resident companies acting directly without a local establishment, direct VAT registration before the SIEE is required using the simplified 'cerfa n°13670' procedure, with documentary proof of economic activity in France; (6) all tax returns and payments must be lodged through the DGFIP professional messaging service 'Espace Professionnel Securisé'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SAS is a corporation resident in France subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) on worldwide profits, with territorial scope limited to profits attributable to French establishments and activities actually carried out in France; the commercial-law autonomy of the SAS does not alter its tax transparency status; it is a separate taxpayer from its shareholders.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SAS may not elect partnership-style pass-through taxation, but French law provides the following elections: (1) optional IR (Impôt sur le Revenu) income-tax transparency for SAS/SARL family companies with fewer than 50 shareholders under article 239 bis AA CGI for a maximum of 5 fiscal years; (2) election for parent-subsidiary group integration ('régime d'intégration fiscale') under article 223 A CGI, allowing the parent SAS to consolidate the results of at least 95%-owned French subsidiaries; (3) election for the group VAT regime (option de groupe TVA) under article 1693 ter CGI, permitting a single VAT taxpayer group; (4) no US-style 'check-the-box' election exists, but anti-hybrid mismatch rules under articles 212 bis A through 212 bis H CGI (ATAD implementation) re-characterize disregarded entities and permanent establishments with no elective effect for entity classification; (5) R&D tax credit ('crédit d'impôt recherche') and reduced-tier IS rates are statutory not elective; (6) fiscal year can be elected to depart from the calendar year but must be declared to DGFIP.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), governed by articles 256 to 289 septies CGI and integrated with EU VAT Directives.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The French domestic small-business TVA exemption (franchise en base) applies to taxable turnover of EUR 85,000 for supply of goods (including manufacturing and distance sales) and EUR 37,500 for supply of services, but manufacture and intra-Community acquisitions of robotic floor-cleaning appliances require mandatory registration if the EU-wide distance-selling threshold of EUR 10,000 (annual cross-border B2C distance sales) is exceeded; any foreign supplier holding stock in France or using a French fulfilment warehouse is subject to mandatory French VAT registration from the first euro regardless of turnover; non-EU suppliers with goods sold via a marketplace may be registered under the non-union OSS scheme or subject to deemed-supplier rules under article 283 CGI (effectively no minimum turnover threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing a mandatory domestic B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting regime under the Finance Act for 2024 (article 279 LPF), as restructured by the ordinance of 17 September 2024, with phased entry into force: mandatory e-invoicing issuance and receipt for large enterprises from 1 September 2026, and for mid-size and small enterprises (including SAS manufacturers) from 1 September 2027; all invoices must be exchanged through one of the Government-approved 'Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires' (PDP) or through the public portal 'Portail Public de Facturation' (PPF / Chorus Pro); each invoice must transmit structured business data and tax data (FACTUR-X, UBL 2.x, CII formats) to the PPF, which performs real-time fiscal clearance, validation and circuit transmission; e-reporting of transaction and payment data (outside the invoicing chain) is mandatory in parallel; invoices must additionally conform to French authentication and archiving requirements (article 289 CGI), and digital stamping is not generally required for VAT receipts in France, but the PPF automatically validates the invoicer's TVA status and SIREN.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating under article 262 CGI applies to supplies of goods that are physically transported outside the EU by the seller or on behalf of the seller, provided the seller retains documentary proof of the export, including the customs export declaration and transport documents evidencing departure of the goods from French customs territory within the statutory deadline; intra-Community supplies of goods (articles 262 ter CGI, 258 A CGI) are equally zero-rated when the purchaser communicates a valid EU VAT identification number and the goods are dispatched to another Member State; supply of offshore services (including assembly, repair, software and technical consulting relating to robotic appliances for non-EU clients) falls under the B2B reverse-charge rule of article 283-2 CGI and is zero-rated when the customer is identified for VAT in another country; export VAT zero-rating may additionally benefit from the 'export cash-flow scheme' set out in article 262 CGI for exporters with regular operations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane, DAU/ENS, including the electronic summary export declaration in DELTA-G or DES), Bill of Lading (Connaissement) or CMR consignment note or Air Waybill, Inward Remittance Certificate (attestation de rapatriement des devises / bank credit advice evidencing receipt of foreign currency payment on French territory)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to heightened DGFIP audit scrutiny through cross-referencing of the export file, the customs export summary and the incoming foreign-currency remittance; if the exporter cannot produce the statutory proof bundle, DGFIP re-characterises the supply as domestic, assesses the full 20% VAT plus late-interest (intérêt de retard at 0.40% per calendar month under article 1727 CGI) and applies the intentional-misconduct penalty of 40% (article 1729 CGI) or the concealment-of-activity penalty of 80% in case of dissimulated export fictions; fraudulent arrangement to obtain unjustified export VAT refunds or zero-rating invokes article 1788 A CGI penalty of EUR 750 per false document, the abuse-of-law procedure (abus de droit, article L.64 LPF) allowing assessment on the actual economic substance, solidary liability of the exporter and the fiscal representative under article 283 CGI, and a potential criminal fine of EUR 37,500 plus five years' imprisonment under articles 1741-1743 CGI for fraudulent VAT evasion; refunds already paid are retrospectively clawed back with penalties for up to six years (or ten years in case of offshore concealment).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), with the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) and Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking supervision; foreign exchange administration under Article L511-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of result
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or sole shareholder of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a court-authorized extension applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late approval may expose officers to liability and prevent timely filing. France has no automatic annual-return strike-off mechanism.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing, including balance sheet, income statement, notes, and management report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the French one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the accounts, or within two months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction may be issued; failure to comply may result in a civil fine of up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance. Repeated registry deficiencies may lead to formal dissolution or RCS radiation proceedings, but no automatic annual strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and required tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after the financial year-end, or by the second business day following 1 May for a calendar-year company, subject to the applicable e-filing timetable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest and penalties generally apply, including a 10% surcharge, with higher penalties for deliberate or fraudulent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate local economic contribution compliance, including CFE payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is generally payable by 15 December; the amount is assessed by the tax administration. Additional declarations apply only where specifically required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment may trigger a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest. No separate annual franchise filing or automatic strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the French one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual confirmation is required. Changes to beneficial ownership or control must generally be reported within 30 days after the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate filing may result in criminal penalties, court injunctions, and restrictions affecting registry compliance. No annual confirmation-based strike-off rule applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of three thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover excluding tax, and 50 average employees. Additional mandatory-audit rules may apply to parent or subsidiary companies in qualifying corporate groups.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French statutory accounts must generally comply with the French Accounting Standards Authority framework and French GAAP. IFRS may be used for qualifying consolidated accounts; it does not generally replace French GAAP for standalone statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a routine annual UBO confirmation. The company must maintain accurate beneficial ownership information and file an amendment generally within 30 days after any change in ownership, control, or identifying information. Share transfers must be recorded in the company's share-transfer register and individual shareholder accounts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share transfers and shareholder accounts
Shareholders' decisions and meeting minute book
Register of directors and corporate officers
Beneficial ownership documentation and supporting control analysis

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 330-1,650 per year, depending on the city and services included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,650-6,600 per year for a small SAS, subject to transaction volume, group structure, and reporting complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard corporate income tax rate of 25%; reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million; research tax credit (CIR) at 30% for eligible R&D expenditures up to EUR 100 million and 5% above; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% for SMEs up to EUR 400,000 of eligible innovation expenditure; 3.3% social surcharge applied to corporate income tax due exceeding EUR 2.5 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (Cerfa No. 15950*06) with attachments 2065 bis-SD, 2058-SD, 2059-SD and statutory annual accounts forms 2050 to 2057; filed electronically through EDI/EFI on impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with four quarterly advance corporate tax payments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; final balance due with the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ending on 31 December: file by 3 May, or the second business day after 1 May if the statutory date falls on a weekend or holiday; other fiscal year-ends: file within three months of the close of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification: SIREN number, NAF/APE code (2750 for domestic appliance manufacture, NAICS 335210 equivalence), SAS legal form, share capital, registered office address and French tax identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS must state its head office in France and identify the legal representative empowered to respond to the tax administration; non-resident corporate shareholders are not individually reported unless the French entity operates as a qualifying permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year opening and closing dates, accounting method, and indication of whether the accounts are prepared in EUR under the French general accounting plan.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the closing date aligns with the foreign parent's consolidation cycle if the French SAS is wholly owned; all amounts must be declared in EUR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation between accounting net income and taxable corporate income: add-back of non-deductible expenses, deductibility of accelerated depreciation, application of tax credits, incorporation of prior-year losses and adjustments for arm's length transfers with related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-managed entities must maintain transfer pricing files evidencing the remuneration of management fees, commissionaire arrangements and trademark licences with the French distributor-manufacturer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 25% headline rate or the 15% reduced SME rate, social surcharge if applicable, and reduction of the final tax due by credits such as CIR and CII.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced SME rate is unavailable where the foreign parent alone or with related parties exceeds EUR 10 million revenue or where the French entity is part of a large corporate group.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of prior-year tax losses carried forward and current-year deficit utilisable to offset future taxable profits, with the annual offset limited to EUR 1 million plus 50% of surplus taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be documented through audited French accounts; losses of the French SAS cannot be consolidated offshore unless the French tax integration regime has been elected and the foreign parent is in France.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic 10% penalty on the net tax due plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.20%; failure to file after formal notice: 40%; intentionally concealed activity or abusive understatement: 80%; non-payment of the balance within 30 days adds a 5% collection surcharge and enables enforced recovery.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must submit a valid French-form tax residence certificate (form 5000, endorsed by the foreign tax authority) and a beneficial ownership declaration to the French paying company or financial agent before the distribution date in order to apply the reduced DTA withholding at source. Where the statutory dividend withholding tax has been deducted but the DTA allows a lower rate, the non-resident must file a refund claim with the DGFIP within the normal revenue-claim window, generally no later than 31 December of the second year following the income event, attaching the residence certificate, dividend voucher and computation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory French withholding tax of 25% on outbound licensing fees for patents, trademarks, know-how and software rights used in France; treaty rates typically range from 0% to 10%, and the EU Interest and Royalties Directive may exempt qualifying related-company royalties. Interest: ordinary arm's length interest paid by a French borrower to non-resident lenders is not subject to French withholding tax; certain bond interest under Article 125 A of the CGI and payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions may trigger a 25% withholding, with treaty reduction usually available.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million in annual turnover or total balance sheet plus more than 100 employees triggers the mandatory French Local File; the Master File becomes mandatory when the worldwide consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 750 million. During audit, the DGFIP may demand local transactions documentation for French related-party flows exceeding EUR 100,000 even if the full documentation threshold is not met.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies no autonomous Economic Substance Regulations comparable to United Arab Emirates or Bermuda; however, the French abuse-of-law doctrine (Article L64 of the LPF), EU anti-hybrid rules, CFC legislation and BEPS Action 6 principal-purpose test require real offices, employees, business equipment and management decisions in France to support low-risk distributor or contract-manufacturer characterisation and to secure treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately filing false corporate tax returns, maintaining double books, suppressing invoices, or diverting robotic vacuum appliance sales into foreign bank accounts without declaration and with no operational counterpart in France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties of 40% for serious understatement, increasing to 80% for abusive or concealed operations, plus late-payment interest at 0.20% monthly. Criminal sanctions: up to five years' imprisonment and EUR 250,000 fine for de jure and de facto directors; aggravated fraud committed in an organised group or online raises the sanctions to seven years' imprisonment and EUR 500,000 fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the SAS president who instigate or conceal fraud may be declared jointly and severally liable for corporate income tax, penalties and interest; judicial travel bans, asset seizure, confiscation and imprisonment are available, with referral to the Comité national de lutte contre la fraude for criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Law (Article L64 LPF)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a French SAS with no staff, no leased premises, no operational management and no genuine commercial activity solely to re-invoice robotic vacuum sales, hold IP or channel royalties/dividends under favourable DTA treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the arrangement as an abuse of law, 80% penalty on the additional tax resulting from the concealed purpose, statutory interest, and denial of treaty benefits; transactions are re-taxed as if the artificial entity did not exist, including additional withholding tax on undisclosed profit distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The de facto or de jure directors who established the artificial shell are jointly and severally liable for the recomputed tax, withholding tax, penalties and interest; criminal courts may impose fines, travel bans, confiscation and imprisonment where the shell is used to facilitate tax fraud or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / Tax Fraud Proceeds (Article 324-1 Code Pénal)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the French robotic vacuum entity to channel inflated commissions, circular payments, cash deposits or crypto conversions through opaque intermediaries for the purpose of concealing the true origin, nature or ownership of taxable profits or evaded customs duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: For natural persons: up to five years' imprisonment and EUR 375,000 fine; for legal persons: a corporate fine equal to five times the statutory natural-person fine, together with confiscation of moveable and immovable property; failure to comply with suspicious transaction reporting obligations may additionally trigger financial-administrative sanctions and TRACFIN enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A president or compliance manager who knowingly participates in, directs or facilitates the laundering scheme may be prosecuted as principal or accomplice, with personal imprisonment, fines, confiscation, disqualification from managing companies, travel bans during investigation, and civil restitution to the State for taxes and penalties evaded.
